name: Edward Heath
summary: Heath was a One Nation Conservative who took Britain into the European Community and remained a committed European to the end. His government mixed tax cuts and union reform with statutory pay and price controls. He opposed the death penalty and later criticised privatisation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1970 manifesto promises to improve the NHS; in 1986 Heath said more resources should go to health.

public-ownership.rationale: The 1970 manifesto says it is totally opposed to further nationalisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The 1970 manifesto promises substantial cuts in income tax and surtax.

decide-locally.rationale: The 1970 manifesto promises to devolve government so more decisions are made locally.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The Immigration Act 1971 set one system of control over entry; only its contents page is read, so the answer is medium.

central-planning.rationale: In 1976 Heath spoke of the extraordinary extent of human fallibility in planning.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: In 1977 Heath praised the institution of monarchy.

direct-votes.rationale: In 1993 and 1996 Heath opposed referendums on the EU and the single currency.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: In 1996 Heath said people whose religious convictions forbid divorce are not entitled in Parliament to impose their belief on other members of the community.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1970 manifesto says all citizens should be equal before the law without discrimination; the Immigration Act 1971 (patrial rules) is not read here, so medium.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The 1970 manifesto gives priority to those most in need.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Heath government enacted the Industrial Relations Act 1971 and sought to curb union power (Britannica); only the Act's contents page is read, so low.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: As Prime Minister Heath defended internment in Northern Ireland in 1971 while promising to phase it out in 1972; the points differ, so low.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Heath said it is right to share sovereignty with European neighbours (2001) and that sovereignty exists for the people's benefit (1996).

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Heath defended permanent NATO membership as justified in 1996, and his 1970 manifesto commits to NATO.

death-penalty.rationale: Heath said in 1983 he had opposed capital punishment for all homicide for over twenty years and always voted against it.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The 1970 manifesto accepts the UNCTAD aid target and promises to increase aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The 1970 manifesto he led commits to independent control of Britain's nuclear weapons.

collective-defense.rationale: Heath defended NATO membership as a justified surrender of sovereignty (1996); he did not address the all-for-one clause itself.

common-currency.rationale: On 23 Feb 1999 and 27 Oct 1997 Heath welcomed the single currency and argued that a single market needs one currency.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: In 1996 Heath argued against reintroducing fault in divorce.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The Heath government enacted the European Communities Act 1972, whose s.2 gave Community law priority in UK law.

defeat-communism.rationale: In 1988 Heath praised the 1963-79 détente and criticised abusing the Soviet Union for no point.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: In 1996 Heath called privatisation dogma wrong and said it aims at profit, not service.

social-market-economy.rationale: The 1970 manifesto pairs tax cuts and opposition to nationalisation with pensions as of right and improving the NHS.

rich-first.rationale: The 1970 manifesto calls regional development policy vital and aims at prosperity in every part of the country.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Heath defended NATO membership (1996) and the manifesto commits to it; he did not speak on neutrality as such.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: On 24 Mar 1972 Heath announced an active, permanent and guaranteed role for the minority in Northern Ireland.

second-chamber.rationale: In 1999 Heath wanted an elected upper house alongside an elected lower house.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The 1970 manifesto keeps nuclear weapons under independent control.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: On 24 Mar 1972 Heath announced periodic border plebiscites in Northern Ireland.

troops-home-from-abroad.rationale: The 1970 manifesto deplores Labour's withdrawal from the Gulf and the Far East.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: The Heath government enacted the Counter-Inflation Act 1973 with statutory power over prices and pay; only its contents page is read, so medium.

notes: Record covers European, defence, Northern Ireland and economic policy; most social and technology statements have no recorded position. Industrial Relations Act and Counter-Inflation Act sources are contents pages only.
